what: The real name lists the people generator draws the city's names from (people.rules.json names.lists): one file per country, <country>.json, written by tools/people/names/extract.py from the downloads below. Given names by sex and decade of birth (born 1940-2009), most common first, with counts; family names most common first, with counts. The lists keep their top 3; the generator skips them by rule. No model reads, writes or picks a name.
untrusted: The downloads are untrusted data. They were fetched into a folder of their own (out/scratch/pulse/names-dl/<country>/, not committed) and only read as tables by extract.py, run with python -I from outside that folder. Each country file records the sha256 of every download it was cut from (`files`).

given.title: Popular baby names, top 1,000 per sex and year, 1880-2008 (Social Security card applications)
given.licence: US federal government work, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). The SSA site refused a scripted download (HTTP 403), so the file is Hadley Wickham's published copy of the same SSA lists (year, name, share of births, sex); it ends at 2008.
given.age: by year of birth: a person's decade of birth sets the list

family.title: Frequently occurring surnames from the 2010 Census (162,253 names with 100 or more bearers)
family.licence: US federal government work, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105)
family.note: the table writes names in capitals without punctuation; extract.py restores Mc- and a short list of O'- names (O'Brien, O'Connor, ...)

given.title: Fichier des prénoms, édition 2025: births by first name, sex and year, 1900-2024 (national file)
given.licence: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence 2.0 (Etalab); Insee's reuse terms: free reuse with the source named

family.title: Fichier des noms (État civil): births by family name and decade of birth, 1891-2000 (national file, names given 30 times or more)
family.note: counted over births 1941-2000, the decades the city's people were born in

given.title: Nombres más frecuentes por fecha de nacimiento: the 50 most frequent names per sex and decade of birth (Padrón Continuo, 1 Jan 2022)
given.licence: CC BY 4.0 (the INE site footer links CC BY 4.0, though its tooltip says CC BY-SA 4.0; either allows reuse with the source named)
given.age: by decade of birth, but only 50 names per decade and sex; compound names (María Carmen, José Antonio) are left out, as a name is one word, so a decade keeps 26 to 50
given.note: INE writes names in capitals without accents, so the city's Spaniards are José and María without the accent (Jose, Maria)

family.title: Frecuencia de apellidos: family names with 100 or more bearers as first surname (Censo anual, 1 Jan 2025)
family.note: the first surname only: a city person carries one family name; no accents (Garcia, Martinez)

given.title: Table 10467: born persons by girls' or boys' name and year, 1880-2025 (names used by 200 or more)
given.licence: CC BY 4.0 (SSB's terms for its statistics bank)

family.title: Table 12891: last names used by 200 persons or more, 2025

given.title: BE0001T100: first names normally used, the 100 most common for women and men on 31 Dec 2021, by year of birth 1922-2021
given.age: by year of birth, but only among the 200 names most common today, so a decade holds 73 to 95 per sex and the oldest decades miss names that have since gone out of use

family.title: BE0001ENamn10: last names with at least 10 bearers, 31 Dec 2020

pins.title: BE0001TNamn10: first names normally used with at least 10 bearers, 2020: Milena, Inez, Arthur, Aleksander, Uros
pins.note: the evidence that each of the five pinned names is a given and a family name of one country (rule: same country): all five are borne in Sweden, by the counts here and in BE0001ENamn10 2020. The US tables also hold Inez (SSA, 1940s-1970s) with Nikolaou (178 bearers in 2010), and Reilly, Popovic, Lukac and Rask.

given.title: Lista imion występujących w rejestrze PESEL (first names of living people, first name, men and women), 31 Jan 2023; and Imiona nadane dzieciom w Polsce 2000-2019 (first names given to children)
given.age: NOT by year of birth for people born before 2000: the register of the living has no year, so every decade 1940-1990 draws from the names of the living, all ages together (weighted to the middle-aged, who are most of them); the 2000s draw from the names given 2000-2009

family.title: Nazwiska występujące w rejestrze PESEL: family names of living men and of living women, 20 Jan 2026
family.note: Polish family names have a man's and a woman's form (Kowalski, Kowalska): a person draws from the list of their sex; a family's name is drawn once from the men's list and a woman of the family carries its woman's form (-ski, -cki, -dzki to -ska, -cka, -dzka; other names unchanged)

gaps: No origin outside Europe and the United States has an open national list of given and family names that could be fetched (checked or tried: England and Wales and Ireland publish given names only; Scotland's tables moved and would not download; the Czech ministry stopped publishing in 2017; Finland's DVV files refused a scripted download). The city's people of African, Asian, Middle Eastern and Latin American descent therefore come only through the United States lists (the 2010 Census surnames: Nguyen, Hernandez, Washington, Kim ...), with American given names. The old pools' 21 origins are down to 6 countries.
SSA's own site refused the download; the given names come from a published copy of its lists that ends in 2008.
Spain's and Sweden's given-name tables are short per decade (50 and the national top 200); Poland's have no year of birth before 2000.
